fields.description:
# Make the completion-verification close gate survive a large, legitimate ticket

Retyped from `bug` to `task`: the original report ("the close gate blames a missing `agents`
extra") was a real defect and its messaging half has LANDED (change 1027; change 1060 extends it
to the step-budget path, proven live). What remains is a deliberate re-shaping of how the gate
handles size — a design change with rejected alternatives, which is task-shaped work.

## What is PROVEN (measured this session, not inferred)

Repro target: ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56`, whose work is complete and merged, and which still
cannot close.

1. **Context size was never the binding constraint.** 9fd4's assembled context is **34,282 chars
   ≈ 8,570 tokens** (reproduced byte-for-byte against the live failure). The verifier model
   `claude-sonnet-4-6` is recorded in this repo's own model-window ladder at **1,000,000 tokens**
   (`plan_review/sizing.py:101`), so the ticket is **~0.86%** of the window and the old
   24,000-char bound was ~0.6%. (An earlier draft of this plan said "~200k window / ~4%" — that
   was WRONG; the corrected figure strengthens the same conclusion.) The bound is a self-imposed
   cost guard, not a capability limit.
2. **The advertised remedy could not work.** Composition: description 10,281 + 9 comments 23,617
   (comments = 69%). Deleting the ENTIRE description still leaves **24,001 chars — one over the
   old limit**. Comments are the only sufficient lever, and the store is append-only:
   `_lib_writes` exposes `comment()` with no delete/redact counterpart.
3. **The two bounds were incoherent.** Criteria ⊂ description ⊂ context, yet
   `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (32,000) > `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (24,000). Proven by sweep: criteria
   totalling 26,000–31,900 chars pass every criteria bound and are then refused on context.
4. **The real blocker for 9fd4 is the STEP budget.** At default settings the primary verifier
   exhausts `max_iterations=480` after ~780s. The runner's `UsageLimitExceeded` arm raises
   **`LLMRunnerError`** (`runner.py:465`), which is NOT an `UnretryableOutputError`, so it falls
   straight through recovery's `except UnretryableOutputError` trap (`completion_recovery.py:405`)
   — the compaction path is unreachable for the very ticket that motivated it.

## Approach

**Compaction becomes a last resort, not the primary mechanism.** Change 1060 currently makes
compaction the normal path at a 40,000-char budget. That is the wrong shape: shipped ticket 19b1
makes ticket **comments** the sanctioned completion-evidence channel, so eliding oldest-first
comments can drop exactly the evidence that proves a criterion and flip a PASS to a FAIL. Because
the real window is 1M tokens, the budget can be set from actual capability so elision never fires
for any realistic ticket.

**Budget derivation (concrete).** Derive the context budget from the repo's EXISTING model-window
ladder — `plan_review/sizing.py`'s `_MODEL_WINDOWS` / `largest_window_tokens` — rather than a new
hardcoded number, so it tracks the configured verifier model instead of drifting. Recovery
re-sends the context once per criterion, so the budget must be sized per-call, not per-run. Keep
the value overridable by the existing config/env surface; do NOT couple it to a literal model name
in `completion_recovery.py`.

**Widening the recovery entry — the discriminant, stated explicitly.** Catch **`LLMRunnerError`**,
NOT a bare `LLMError`: `LLMUnavailableError` is a SIBLING of `LLMRunnerError` under `LLMError`
(`errors.py:15,29`), so catching `LLMError` would route auth / rate-limit / connection failures
into recovery and burn billable per-criterion evidence calls on a condition where the model cannot
run at all. Gate entry on a predicate symmetric with the existing `_is_token_exhaustion`, and
**reuse the classification `failure.py` already owns** rather than adding a rival local one:
`failure.py:199-200` already disambiguates "a genuine step budget (request_limit)" from a
stuck/looping tool, and maps `UsageLimitExceeded` to `ResolutionClass.FIX_AGENT_DESIGN`
(`failure.py:266-268`). A stuck/looping-tool exhaustion must NOT enter recovery — only a genuine
request-limit exhaustion.

**Alternative rejected — escalate to a larger-context model as the fallback.** It solves a
constraint that is not binding (0.86% of the window). It addresses neither real limit (tool-call
iterations; the separate 16,000 output-token budget), and `completion.py` records a measured
reason it would likely make things WORSE — the framework default (opus) was rejected for this gate
because it "over-explores … blowing the step budget", which is precisely the live failure. It also
makes a signed verdict tier-dependent: the same ticket could pass on one model and fail on
another, a worse property for an attestation gate than for a plain reviewer.

**Alternative rejected — tell authors to prune tickets.** No such policy exists in the repo
predating this bug's own error string, and (2) shows pruning cannot work for a comment-dominated
ticket.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — budget derived from the model-window ladder;
  compaction demoted to last resort with a defined elision marker; recovery entry widened to
  `LLMRunnerError` + a genuine-step-budget predicate reusing `failure.py`'s classification.
- `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — remedy by cause (LANDED
  in 1060; keep, no further change expected).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` §"Bounded completion recovery" — the budgets, the derivation, the
  elision marker, and which failures enter recovery.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py` (new) and
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py` (new). The latter deliberately does not
  duplicate the sibling `test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py`, which already pins the
  bounded-recovery remedy and its negative control; this one covers only the step-budget path.

## Testing

Unit tier with a fake runner (no billable calls) for every bound, branch and entry predicate, plus
one live end-to-end close of 9fd4 at DEFAULT settings as the acceptance oracle. Mutation-verify
each new test by re-introducing the exact mechanism it pins; a test that stays green under that
mutation is a tautology and must be strengthened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a completion-verifier failure that is NOT a missing dependency (specifically a step-budget
      exhaustion, which ran the model) does not tell the operator to install the `agents` extra or
      set an API key, and does surface the remedy the exception itself carries; a genuine
      unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance (negative control)
- [ ] the recovery context budget is derived from the repo's existing model-window ladder
      (`plan_review/sizing.py`), not a new literal, and a test asserts the derivation tracks the
      ladder rather than a hardcoded number
- [ ] a ticket of 9fd4's measured size (34,282 chars) is verified with **zero** characters elided
      — a test asserts the context passed to the model is byte-identical to the assembled context,
      not merely "within budget"
- [ ] when compaction does fire, it drops no criterion returned by `explicit_completion_criteria()`
      (that function's output is the definition of "criterion" for this AC, including the
      synthesized bug-core criterion), and every elision is marked in-band with a fixed,
      documented marker string; one test asserts criteria survival and one asserts the marker is
      present and counts what was removed
- [ ] a genuine step-budget exhaustion (`LLMRunnerError` from the runner's `UsageLimitExceeded`
      arm) enters bounded recovery, and a test pins that entry path
- [ ] `LLMUnavailableError` and a stuck/looping-tool exhaustion do NOT enter recovery — asserted by
      recovery-call count being zero — so widening the catch cannot burn billable calls on
      conditions the model cannot recover from
- [ ] the step-budget entry predicate reuses `failure.py`'s existing `UsageLimitExceeded`
      classification rather than introducing a second, rival classifier; a test pins that a
      change in `failure.py`'s verdict changes the entry decision
- [ ] `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` cannot exceed the context budget — pinned as an invariant test
- [ ] a genuinely unbounded payload still fails fast with ZERO billable recovery calls, asserted
      by call count
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` §"Bounded completion recovery" states the derived budget, the
      elision marker, and which failure classes enter recovery; a test or doc-check asserts the
      documented numbers match the code constants
- [ ] entering recovery and firing compaction each emit an observable signal (log line with the
      measured sizes) so an operator can see from output why a close took the fallback path
- [ ] ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56` closes at DEFAULT settings without `--force-close` and without
      any `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` override, with the command output recorded as a comment here
